title: Origin of Disease and Medicine
subtitle: A story about animals, plants, and human conduct

animals.author: James Mooney
animals.locator: Myth 4 · ORIGIN OF DISEASE AND MEDICINE, normalized characters 353-760
animals.excerpt: This was bad enough, but to make it worse Man invented bows, knives, blowguns, spears, and hooks, and began to slaughter the larger animals, birds, and fishes for their flesh or their skins, while the smaller creatures, such as the frogs and worms, were crushed and trodden upon without thought, out of pure carelessness or contempt. So the animals resolved to consult upon measures for their common safety.

plants.author: James Mooney
plants.locator: Myth 4 · ORIGIN OF DISEASE AND MEDICINE, normalized characters 6412-6772
plants.excerpt: When the Plants, who were friendly to Man, heard what had been done by the animals, they determined to defeat the latters' evil designs. Each Tree, Shrub, and Herb, down even to the Grasses and Mosses, agreed to furnish a cure for some one of the diseases named, and each said: "I shall appear to help Man when he calls upon me in his need." Thus came medicine

narrativeBlocks.title: A council of the animals
narrativeBlocks.body: The animals hold council: humans multiply without limit and kill them carelessly — so, to even the balance, the animals invent diseases to afflict the people.

narrativeBlocks.title: Every beast a sickness
narrativeBlocks.body: Each animal devises its own ailment — the deer brings rheumatism for the hunter who forgets to ask pardon, and the rest follow: a catalog of diseases sent as a judgment.

narrativeBlocks.title: The plants' counter-council
narrativeBlocks.body: Then the plants — friends of humankind — hold their own council, and each offers itself as a cure: every animal's disease, a plant's answer.

narrativeBlocks.title: Medicine as alliance
narrativeBlocks.body: That is why the Cherokee world treats healing as alliance: the plant offers, the healer asks properly, and the cure is the plant keeping its ancient promise.

narrativeBlocks.title: A sacred story, not a remedy
narrativeBlocks.body: This is a Cherokee sacred account collected by James Mooney — it explains the world's moral balance. It is not medical instruction, and it does not validate treatments — the plants' cures belong to the story's own framework.

quiz.prompt: Why do the animals invent diseases?

choices.text: To punish humanity for multiplying and killing them carelessly — a judgment-council

quiz.explanation: Disease is the animals' balancing answer to unchecked hunting.

quiz.prompt: What do the plants offer in their council?

choices.text: Each offers itself as a cure — every animal-made disease gets a plant-made answer
They poison the animals in turn

quiz.explanation: The plants are humanity's allies — the counter to the animal judgment.
